name: Earth's resources, potable water and waste water

terms.definition: A resource that will run out, such as crude oil and metal ores.
terms.examiner: Renewable resources can be replaced as fast as they are used.

terms.definition: Meeting the needs of current generations without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
terms.examiner: Chemistry helps by improving processes and products.

terms.definition: Water that is safe to drink, with low levels of dissolved salts and microbes.
terms.examiner: It is not pure water in the chemical sense.

terms.definition: Filter through filter beds, then sterilise with chlorine, ozone or ultraviolet light.
terms.examiner: In the UK, rain provides fresh water.

terms.definition: Making potable water from salt water by distillation or reverse osmosis (membranes); both need a lot of energy.
terms.examiner: Used where fresh water is scarce.

terms.definition: Screening and grit removal, sedimentation into sludge and effluent, aerobic treatment of effluent, anaerobic digestion of sludge.
terms.examiner: Removes organic matter and harmful microbes.

terms.definition: Plants absorb metal compounds from low-grade ore; they are burned and the ash is processed to get the metal.
terms.examiner: Higher tier. Bioleaching uses bacteria to produce leachate solutions.
